title: Negative Momentum for Convex-Concave Optimization
summary: This paper revisits momentum in the context of min-max optimization. Momentum is a celebrated mechanism for accelerating gradient dynamics in settings like convex minimization, but its direct use in min-max optimization makes gradient dynamics diverge. Surprisingly, Gidel et al. 2019 showed that negative momentum can help fix convergence. However, despite these promising initial results and progress since, the power of momentum remains unclear for min-max optimization in two key ways.
